title: The key-provider bound test asserts wall-clock time and fails under CI contention
description:
Measured on 2026-09-29 while promoting WCLI-51, from a real red rather than from inspection.

test/key-provider.test.ts:293, the load and create cases of describe("every store call settles within its bound"), sets a 150 ms bound and then asserts elapsed >= 140 AND elapsed < 400 on the wall clock, read with performance.now(). The upper number is a lint on scheduler jitter rather than on the code behaviour, so contention alone can break it.

THE INSTANCE. Run 36565512667, the pull_request workflow for SHA 61aa8a24, failed with "(fail) every store call settles within its bound > load gives up at the bound [474.43ms]" — 474 ms against the 400 ms ceiling. Nothing about the change under test was involved: it touched the vault state document, the reporting module, the error catalogue and their tests, none of which is on this timing path.

IT IS A FLAKE, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Three independent readings:
1. The SAME SHA 61aa8a24 passed the push workflow (run 36565482468, conclusion success) while failing the pull_request workflow. Identical bytes, two outcomes.
2. A re-run of the failed job on the same SHA, changing nothing, returned success.
3. The mechanism is visible in the timings. Run 36565482468 ran 12:02:12Z to 12:02:54Z (42 s) and run 36565512667 ran 12:02:28Z to 12:04:05Z (97 s) — they overlapped by 26 seconds on the same runner group, and the contended run took more than twice as long. Every earlier SHA pair in this repository ran sequentially, 40 or more seconds apart, and passed. This is the first pair that raced.

WHY THE CAUSE IS NOT ONLY THE TEST. The overlap happens because a push to dev fires both the push and the pull_request workflows for one SHA, and .github/workflows/ci.yml scopes concurrency per ref, so the two do not cancel each other. That is a CI configuration question and it is deliberately left open here: the test should be robust whether or not the configuration is changed.

THE FIX IS ALREADY IN THE FILE. Two blocks below, the test "the default bound is 10 s and is the one applied" asserts the same kind of bound deterministically by replacing globalThis.setTimeout, recording the delay it was given and asserting on that value. The technique this task needs is therefore eight lines away rather than something to invent, and the wall-clock assertion should either go or be widened far enough that no runner can break it.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN JUST RETRIED. A gate that is re-run whenever it is inconvenient is how a real regression eventually gets waved through, and this one will recur on the next overlapping pair.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The store-call bound is asserted deterministically, or its wall-clock ceiling is wide enough that runner contention cannot break it
The assertion still fails when the provider stops honouring its timeout, proven by mutating the check rather than by observing it green

Every other wall-clock upper bound in the suite that runner contention can break is swept and either widened with a measured margin or made deterministic; the starting list is backup.test.ts:538 (under 2000 ms), setup.test.ts:201 (under 5000 ms) and vault-store.test.ts:626 (under 2000 ms), alongside key-provider.test.ts:293 from the first criterion

plan: Make the key-provider load and create bound deterministic with a shared immediate-timer helper, keeping the configured bound and the refusal as the assertions
Prove the assertion reddens by mutating the provider, not by observing it green: a bound taken from the default instead of the configured value, and a bound applied as Infinity
Same treatment for setup.test.ts unresponsive-store case, whose 5 s ceiling equals Bun default test timeout and so could never fire
Sweep every remaining wall-clock upper bound in the suite, measure each survivor idle and under induced CPU load, and record the margin beside the assertion
Run the full check plus a repeat-run stability pass, open the PR, and close the task with the sweep and mutation evidence
implementationNotes:
SCOPE WIDENED, 2026-09-29, on a relay from opum-agent (OPAG-768, cross-session, 12:41:45Z) and verified here in the source rather than taken on the message. The fleet survey found three more wall-clock ceilings in this suite beyond key-provider.test.ts:293:

- test/backup.test.ts around line 538: expect Date.now() - started toBeLessThan(2_000), the FIFO read-never-blocks bound.
- test/setup.test.ts around line 201: expect performance.now() - started toBeLessThan(5_000), the unresponsive-store bound.
- test/vault-store.test.ts around line 626: expect performance.now() - started toBeLessThan(2_000), the vault-busy bound.

All three verified by reading the lines. They differ in shape from the instance this task was filed for: each asserts an upper bound only, with no lower bound, so contention alone can still break them when a starved runner pushes a correct operation past the ceiling, but there is no jitter window to also fall short of. The fix is the same family, which is why they are one task rather than a new one; a third acceptance criterion now names them and asks for the rest of the suite to be swept in the same pass.

REVIEW AND CLOSE. Independent review (opum-workflow reviewer) at 812e879 found 4 findings plus 2 informational; a re-verification pass at 087b3ab confirmed the four fixes and raised 3 residuals, of which two are now closed (F6 fixed, F3 residual closed in the helper header) and one is a correction to this record (F7, below).

- F1 medium, fixed in 087b3ab: making the bound deterministic had dropped the only upper wall-clock bound on the store-call path — measured by the reviewer, a 600 ms delay added to read() outside globalThis.setTimeout left the old form red at 754.91 ms and the new one green. A 1 s ceiling (6.7x the configured bound) now sits beside the delays and readAttempts assertions. Measured band: Bun.sleep(1500) in read() reddens it (Received 1504.0), 600 ms does not; the reviewer reproduced the edge between 900 and 1100 ms and judged 1 s right. Loaded cost of the wrapped call: 0.15-11.6 ms over 15 runs at 6x CPU overcommit, so the ceiling has about 86x headroom over the worst induced reading.
- F3 low, fixed in 087b3ab: the fake fired its handler inline, so run(signal) began with an aborted signal. Now queued as a microtask; measured, abortedAtEntry false and the refusal still vault_key_unavailable. Residual closed in 2329c2d: the handler still wins the race against a call that settles normally, so the helper header now says it must wrap a fixture that cannot settle, which both call sites do (hang mode).
- F4 low, fixed in 087b3ab and worse than reported: restore() captured the real timer per install, so a nested install captured the OUTER FAKE and a non-LIFO pair of restores left a fake installed (measured: a 50 ms sleep costing 0 ms after both restores). Originals are now captured at module load and each restore acts only if its own fake is installed; measured 0 ms while installed, 51-53 ms after both. Two boundary cases (a foreign wrapper displaced by ours, and what is installed at first import) are stated in the header; neither is reachable here.
- F5 low, fixed: both kept bounds now carry the measurement (0-1 ms and 67-76 ms, idle and at 2x and 6x CPU overcommit) rather than the claim.
- F6 info, FIXED in 2329c2d rather than deferred: the vault-busy case now asserts a floor (waited >= 50, the configured busy timeout) as well as the 2 s ceiling. The reason given for deferring it was wrong and the reviewer said so: a floor on that wait cannot flake, because contention only lengthens it. Measured: with PRAGMA busy_timeout forced to 0 the refusal code is still vault_busy and the wait is 0.304 ms, and the floor reddens — a class neither the ceiling nor the code assertion could see.
- F7 info, a correction to this record: this note originally cited the sweep sites as backup.test.ts:538, setup.test.ts:201 and vault-store.test.ts:626 with the words All three verified by reading the lines. The citations were accurate for the tree they were read against; the WCLI-52 diff shifted backup.test.ts, so :538 now points into the restore tests and the FIFO bound it names is at :731 post-change. setup.test.ts:201 and vault-store.test.ts:626 were correct as written. Line-number citations go stale when a file above them changes, so this task names its sites by what they assert. Both this correction and F6 are also stated in commits 2329c2d and the closing note, after the reviewer flagged that an earlier commit message claimed them recorded while the record was still untouched.

MUTATION PROOF (AC2): with the provider taking its bound from defaultKeyTimeoutMs instead of the configured value the delay assertion fails in 0.41 ms; with the bound applied as Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY both cases fail in under 1 ms; with read() delayed by Bun.sleep(1500) the restored ceiling fails; a retry re-arming the bound fails on delays length, which the old wall-clock window passed; an unapplied busy timeout fails the new floor at 0.304 ms.

STABILITY: 5 repeat runs of key-provider + setup, 70 pass each, and 5/5 under 6x CPU overcommit; the full suite 649 pass 0 fail in 25.6-26.2 s.

SWEEP (AC3): key-provider.test.ts and setup.test.ts made deterministic; the backup.test.ts FIFO bound (0-1 ms measured) and the vault-store.test.ts vault-busy bound (67-76 ms measured) kept, with their bands measured and now written beside them, the vault-busy one floored as well as ceilinged; every other toBeLessThan or toBeGreaterThan in test/, test/qualification, scripts/ and evals/ bounds a count, a size or a fraction, not time.

FILED: WCLI-57 (a push to dev runs both CI workflows for one SHA and their concurrency groups differ, which is what put two jobs on one runner and stretched the bound). It rides in this PR as a tracker-only addition rather than waiting for its own branch.

CHECKS: bun run check green (the 3 lint warnings pre-existing); lore check and lore validate --strict exit 0; CI green on 812e879, 087b3ab and 2329c2d, with run 36590629639 covering the final code and tests.
finalSummary:
The store-call bound is asserted rather than waited out, and the same treatment went to every wall-clock bound in the suite.

test/support/immediate-timers.ts replaces globalThis.setTimeout with one that fires as a microtask and records the delay it was given. key-provider.test.ts load and create now assert the configured 150 ms bound was applied and that firing it produces vault_key_unavailable, with readAttempts 1, writeAttempts 0, plus a 1 s ceiling that covers latency added outside setTimeout. setup.test.ts unresponsive-store case asserts the configured 2 s bound the same way, keeping the indeterminate exit, exitExplicitly and unchanged-vault assertions; its old 5 s ceiling equalled the default test timeout, so it could only race the harness. The two bounds that stay wall-clock were measured rather than assumed: the FIFO read (0-1 ms) and the vault-busy wait (67-76 ms against a 50 ms busy timeout), idle and at 2x and 6x CPU overcommit, and the vault-busy case now carries a floor as well as a ceiling, which is the one shape the original flake cannot break and which catches a busy timeout that stopped being applied (measured: PRAGMA busy_timeout = 0 leaves the code vault_busy and the wait at 0.304 ms).

VERIFIED by mutating the subject rather than observing green: a provider taking its bound from the default fails the assertion in 0.41 ms; a bound applied as Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY fails both cases in under 1 ms; a retry re-arming the bound fails on delays length, which the old wall-clock window passed; 1.5 s of added real latency fails the restored ceiling; an unapplied busy timeout fails the new floor. Five repeat runs of both rewritten files, 70 pass each, and 5/5 under 6x CPU overcommit; the full suite 649 pass 0 fail. Independent review raised four findings plus two informational, all reproduced and fixed, with a re-verification pass confirming each and two residuals closed. Delivered in opum-ai/ward-cli#112; CI run 36590629639 green on 2329c2d covers the code and tests. WCLI-57 was filed for the CI overlap that produced the original red.
